project: WO-C3 — Add Reasoning-Effort and File-Backed Prompt Parity to you run
description: Make one-shot ad-hoc you run invocations accept the canonical worker reasoning-effort override and an exact UTF-8 prompt from --to-file, with strict pre-dispatch source validation, preserved existing invocation behavior, synchronized CLI/help/reference contracts, and deterministic end-to-end proof.

context.customerAsk: Add --worker-reasoning-effort and --to-file <path> to ad-hoc you run so AGY or Codex workers can receive a supported explicit effort and one exact long or multiline prompt without fragile shell quoting; reject invalid or conflicting sources before dispatch, preserve current run and Factory-signature behavior, publish the canonical contract, and deliver through merged terminal-green CI.
context.problem: The live generic you run path rejects --worker-reasoning-effort even though authored Workers support canonical reasoning effort, while PowerShell Start-Process can split a multiline --to value into many positional arguments and cause INVOCATION_ARGUMENT_POSITIONAL_OVERFLOW. Long ad-hoc probes and explicit effort are therefore unreliable.
context.solution: Declare canonical run-scoped effort and file-backed prompt inputs; reuse the authored Worker effort canonicalization and existing Worker request field; resolve --to-file through Work-owned input policy and an injected filesystem boundary; preserve exact UTF-8 content; reject conflicts, bad files, unsupported effort, and disallowed run shapes before Provider dispatch; then regenerate and verify CLI/help/reference surfaces with focused functional tests.

acceptanceCriteria: you run --worker-reasoning-effort <supported-value> accepts the canonical authored-Worker effort vocabulary, normalizes it consistently, and carries it in the existing Worker request through dispatch; an unsupported value exits non-zero with an actionable diagnostic and no provider dispatch.

you run --to-file <path> reads a non-empty valid UTF-8 regular file and delivers its complete contents, including spaces, original line endings, non-ASCII characters, and trailing newline, as exactly one logical prompt without shell argv transport or content normalization.

--to-file, signature-defined --to, positional invocation text, and supplied non-empty stdin are mutually exclusive; conflicts, invalid paths/files/encoding/content, and run shapes without a primary prompt fail non-zero before runtime or Provider dispatch with source-specific diagnostics.

Invocations that omit the new flags preserve ordinary --to, stdin, positional Factory input, Factory-signature named/file/repeated/default inputs, packaged Factory behavior, batch/current/JavaScript run shapes, output behavior, and Provider-specific effort validation.

Canonical CLI sources and generated consumers, you run --help, and packaged you docs run describe the flags, strict conflict rule, effort semantics, and an independently runnable you run --provider codex --worker-reasoning-effort xhigh --to-file <path> example.

Applicable typecheck, focused unit/integration/functional tests, generated-contract checks, and documentation smoke checks pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, every blocking PR conversation item is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file changes are reconciled, and the PR is actually merged; opened, green, approved, or ready-to-merge is not complete.

userStories.title: Apply explicit reasoning effort to ad-hoc worker dispatch
userStories.description: As a customer running an ad-hoc worker, I want to select its reasoning effort explicitly so the worker executes with the intended supported effort instead of rejecting or ignoring my request.
acceptanceCriteria: --worker-reasoning-effort is a typed you run input for applicable one-shot worker invocations and accepts the same normalized canonical values as authored Worker configuration, without a parallel enum, aliases, or fallback-to-default behavior.

A supported value, including existing case and whitespace normalization, reaches the existing Worker execution request reasoning-effort field and is observable at the deterministic Provider command edge.

A globally unsupported value fails non-zero before Factory Session activation or Provider dispatch with an actionable diagnostic naming the value; a canonically valid but Provider-unsupported value continues through existing Provider-specific rejection.
Omitting the flag preserves authored Worker/provider/model defaults, and existing packaged Factory effort signature parameters continue to work.
Focused CLI and functional regressions prove accepted effort dispatch and pre-dispatch rejection through root.BuildProcess and Process.Execute with Provider effects replaced only through edges.Edges.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented and verified the typed run-scoped override. Canonicalization, pre-dispatch rejection, hosted and detached invocation forwarding, authored-effort fallback, and the deterministic Codex command edge are covered by focused unit and root.BuildProcess/Process.Execute functional tests.

userStories.title: Deliver one exact prompt from --to-file
userStories.description: As a customer with a long or multiline brief, I want you run to read the prompt from a file so shell quoting cannot split or alter it.
acceptanceCriteria: --to-file <path> is accepted for run shapes with one logical primary text prompt, including applicable ad-hoc AGY and Codex worker invocations, and paths containing spaces resolve through the existing injected filesystem boundary.

The selected path must identify a readable regular file containing valid, logically non-empty UTF-8; failure identifies the source/path, exits non-zero, and occurs before Factory Session activation or Provider dispatch.

File contents reach one Provider request with spaces, Unicode, original CR/LF sequences, blank lines, and final newline preserved, without trimming, joining, newline conversion, or argv re-tokenization.

--to-file conflicts with signature-defined --to, positional prompt input, and supplied non-empty stdin; every combination returns the stable invocation-input conflict classification, names the sources, and never silently chooses precedence.

Run shapes without a primary prompt reject --to-file, while invocation without it preserves existing stdin, positional, ordinary --to, and signature-defined named/file/repeated/default argument behavior.

A functional regression uses a real 30-line UTF-8 prompt file at a path containing spaces and proves exact single-prompt delivery through ProviderCommandRunner; conflict and unreadable-file regressions prove zero dispatch.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented Work-owned --to-file preparation with injected regular-file inspection and reading, UTF-8/non-empty validation, exact text preservation, stable file/named/positional/stdin source conflicts, signature primary-parameter routing, and pre-dispatch rejection for non-prompt run shapes. Added generated CLI contract wiring and root.BuildProcess functional regressions proving a real 30-line UTF-8 file at a path with spaces reaches one Codex ProviderCommandRunner request byte-for-byte; conflict, missing-file, and non-regular-file cases prove zero dispatch and no read for invalid metadata. Focused Work/CLI/wire tests, make test, and lifecycle tests pass.

acceptanceCriteria: The authored CLI manifest declares both flags, applicability, and --to-file conflicts, and all generated CLI manifest/consumer artifacts are regenerated through source-of-truth workflows without hand editing.

you docs run includes a PowerShell-safe workflow ending in you run --provider codex --worker-reasoning-effort xhigh --to-file "<path with spaces>", with prompt content absent from argv.
The documented command is independently runnable against the built CLI, and its deterministic test form proves the real 30-line prompt and xhigh effort reach one Codex worker dispatch together.
CLI contract/help tests and make docs-reference-smoke prove customer-visible behavior and packaged reference rendering without source-inventory or link-topology meta-tests.
